extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants, recipients, institutional research administrators, and grants management staff
extracted.subtask_description: A glossary of terms, definitions, and policy-level requirements used throughout the NIH Grants Policy Statement to guide application preparation, award administration, compliance, and reporting. It defines standards and examples that determine allowability, responsibilities, and procedures for NIH-funded grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowability of Salaries and Wages
rubrics_metrics.description: Salary may not be increased as a result of replacing organizational salary funds with NIH grant funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Cost Considerations—Allowability of Costs/Activities—Selected Items of Cost—Salaries and Wages for detailed policy and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Review Board
rubrics_metrics.description: An administrative body established to protect the rights and welfare of human research subjects recruited to participate in research activities conducted under the auspices of the organization with which it is affiliated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IRB has the authority to approve, require modifications in, or disapprove all research activities that fall within its jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: IHE
rubrics_metrics.description: IHE is defined at 20 U.S.C. 1001.

rubrics_metrics.name: Property having no physical existence (intangible property)
rubrics_metrics.description: Property having no physical existence, such as trademarks, copyrights, data (including data licenses), websites, IP licenses, trade secrets, patents, patent applications and property, such as loans, notes and other debt instruments, lease agreements, stocks and other instruments of property ownership of either tangible or intangible property, such as intellectual property, software, or software subscriptions or licenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intergovernmental Personnel Act Mobility Program
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides for the temporary assignment of personnel between the Federal Government and state and local governments, colleges and universities, Indian tribe (or 'federally recognized Indian tribe') governments, federally funded research and development centers, and other eligible organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goal is to facilitate short-term movement of employees when it serves a sound public purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal control over compliance requirements for Federal awards
rubrics_metrics.description: A process implemented by recipients and subrecipients designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the achievement of objectives for a Federal award, including: (1) Transactions are properly recorded and accounted for to permit preparation of reliable financial statements and Federal reports, maintain accountability over assets, and demonstrate compliance with Federal statutes, regulations, and award terms; (2) Transactions are executed in compliance with Federal statutes, regulations, and award terms that could have a direct and material effect on a Federal program and any other Federal statutes/regulations identified in the Compliance Supplement; (3) Funds, property, and other assets are safeguarded against loss from unauthorized use or disposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes the specific three objective categories and the requirement that internal controls provide reasonable assurance for each.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal controls
rubrics_metrics.description: A process, implemented by recipients and subrecipients, designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the achievement of objectives in these categories: (1) Effectiveness and efficiency of operations; (2) Reliability of reporting for internal and external use; (3) Compliance with applicable laws and regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: International organization
rubrics_metrics.description: An organization that identifies itself as international or intergovernmental and has membership from, and represents the interests of, more than one country, without regard to whether the headquarters of the organization and location of the activity are inside or outside of the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement pursuant to 37 CFR Part 401 that recipients of contracts, grants or cooperative agreements fully disclose any subject inventions made during the performance of work under a funding agreement in order to protect the Federal government's rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigational new drug
rubrics_metrics.description: A new drug or biological drug that is used in a clinical investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator-initiated research
rubrics_metrics.description: Research funded as a result of an investigator, on their own, submitting a research application in response to Parent Announcements only. Also known as unsolicited research.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPF number
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional Profile File (IPF) number is a unique number used by NIH for tracking/reporting awards to recipient institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Just-in-Time
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH policy allows the submission of certain elements of a competing application to be deferred until later in the application process, after review when the application is under consideration for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within the Status module of the eRA Commons, users can submit Just-In-Time information when requested by NIH. See Completing the Pre-Award Process—Just-In-Time Procedures for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liquidated damages
rubrics_metrics.description: An amount defined in a contract and chargeable against funds due to the contractor for each day the contractor fails to complete the project beyond the contract completion date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local government
rubrics_metrics.description: Any unit of government within a state, including counties, boroughs, municipalities, cities, towns, townships, parishes, local public authorities (including public housing agencies), special districts, school districts, intrastate districts, councils of governments, and any other agency or instrumentality of a multi-, regional, or intra-state or local government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major A&R (Alteration & Renovation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Alteration and renovation activities are considered modernization activities and are typically supported under research grants where the primary purpose for the grant is other than construction or modernization. The determination of whether proposed A&R is major or minor is made by the NIH Program Official.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major A&R is an unallowable activity or cost under foreign grants and foreign components in domestic grants. See 'Modernization' for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Malign foreign talent recruitment program (MFRTP)
rubrics_metrics.description: As outlined in the CHIPS and Science Act, MFRTP means any program, position, or activity that includes compensation (cash, in-kind, research funding, promised future compensation, complimentary foreign travel, honorific titles, career advancement opportunities, or other remuneration) directly provided by a foreign country or affiliated entity to the targeted individual in exchange for certain activities (e.g., unauthorized transfer of IP or nonpublic information; recruiting trainees; establishing labs/companies/accepting positions violating federal award terms; inability to terminate agreement; limiting capacity to carry out a federal award; requiring application to foreign funding agencies with foreign organization as recipient; omitting acknowledgment of U.S. affiliation or federal sponsor; not disclosing participation to federal agency or employing institution; conflicts of interest/commitment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also defines programs sponsored by a foreign country of concern, certain academic institutions, or listed foreign talent recruitment programs as MFRTPs. Provides examples of activities that are NOT considered MFRTPs unless funded/organized/managed by institutions on specified lists: (1) scholarly presentations and publishing scientific information not otherwise controlled; (2) participation in international conferences/exchanges involving open reciprocal exchange of scientific information; (3) advising or writing recommendations for foreign students at their request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Extramural awards are divided into three types of financial assistance: grants, cooperative agreements and contracts. A mechanism is the type of funded application or transaction used by NIH. Within each mechanism NIH includes programs, which can be further refined by specific activity codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merger
rubrics_metrics.description: A legal action resulting in the unification of two or more legal entities. When such an action involves transfer of NIH grants, procedures for recognizing a successor-in-interest will apply; when it does not involve transfer of NIH grants, procedures for recognizing a name change will apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Data that provide additional information intended to make scientific data interpretable and reusable (e.g., date, independent sample and variable construction and description, methodology, data provenance, data transformations, any intermediate or descriptive observational variables).

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro-purchase
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual procurement transaction for supplies or services using simplified acquisition procedures, the aggregate amount of which does not exceed the micro-purchase threshold. Micro-purchases comprise a subset of a recipient's or subrecipient’s small purchases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Micro-purchase threshold generally does not exceed the amount set by the FAR at 48 CFR Part 2, Subpart 2.1, unless a higher threshold is requested and approved by the cognizant agency for indirect costs. See 2 CFR Part 200.320 for context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor A&R (Alteration & Renovation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Alteration and renovation activities considered modernization activities; determination of whether proposed A&R is major or minor is made by the NIH Program Official.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor A&R is not an allowable activity or cost under grants to individuals or grants for limited purposes (e.g., conference grants). Routine maintenance and repair are not A&R and are typically treated as indirect costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modernization
rubrics_metrics.description: Alteration, renovation, remodeling, improvement, expansion or repair of, or completion of shell space in an existing building necessary to make the building suitable for use for the purposes of a particular program. Modernization is distinct from construction in that it leaves the existing structure in place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the primary purpose of the award is to modernize biomedical research facilities, the grant cannot support the conduct of any research. Examples of Major A&R (e.g., structural change to foundation/roof/floor/exterior load-bearing walls or extension to increase floor area/change function). Examples of Minor A&R include changes to interior dimensions/finishes, installation of fixed equipment (casework, fume hoods, large autoclaves, biosafety cabinets), replacement/removal/reconfiguration of interior non-load bearing walls/doors/windows, making shell space suitable for non-occupancy storage, and accessibility alterations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modified Total Direct Cost (MTDC)
rubrics_metrics.description: All direct salaries and wages, applicable fringe benefits, materials and supplies, services, travel, and subawards up to the first $25,000 of each subaward (regardless of period of performance). MTDC excludes equipment, capital expenditures, patient care charges, rental costs, tuition remission, scholarships and fellowships, participant support costs, and the portion of each subaward in excess of $25,000. Other items may only be excluded when necessary to avoid serious inequity and with cognizant agency approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular application
rubrics_metrics.description: A type of grant application in which support is requested in specified increments without the need for detailed supporting information related to separate budget categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When modular procedures apply, they affect application preparation, review, award, and post-award administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: A process whereby the programmatic and business management performance aspects of a grant are assessed by reviewing information gathered from required reports, audits, site visits, and other sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name change
rubrics_metrics.description: An action whereby the name of an organization is changed without otherwise affecting the rights and obligations of that organization as a recipient.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Investigator
rubrics_metrics.description: A PD/PI who has not previously competed successfully as a PD/PI for a substantial NIH independent research award is considered a New Investigator. For example, a PD/PI who has previously received a competing NIH R01 is no longer a New Investigator; receipt of small grants (R03) or R21 does not disqualify New Investigator status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See list of NIH grants that do not disqualify New Investigator status at the provided URL. See also definition of Early Stage Investigator.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-cost extension
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension of time to a project period and/or budget period to complete the work of the grant under that period, without additional Federal funds or competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See NIH Standard Terms of Award and Prior Approval Requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-competing continuation application/award
rubrics_metrics.description: A financial assistance request (application or progress report) or resulting award for a subsequent budget period within a previously approved project period for which a recipient does not have to compete with other applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Discretionary Award
rubrics_metrics.description: An award made by NIH to specific recipients in accordance with statutory, eligibility and compliance requirements, in which NIH cannot exercise judgment. The award amount could be specifically determined or by formula.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH does not typically make non-discretionary awards. See 'Discretionary Award' for contrast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Federal entity
rubrics_metrics.description: A state, local government, Indian tribe, institution of higher education (IHE), or nonprofit organization that carries out a Federal award as a recipient or subrecipient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Federal share
rubrics_metrics.description: When cost sharing or matching is required as a condition of an award, the portion of allowable project/program costs not borne by the Federal government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-profit organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Any organization that: (1) Is operated primarily for scientific, educational, service, charitable, or similar purposes in the public interest; (2) Is not organized primarily for profit; (3) Uses net proceeds to maintain, improve, or expand operations; (4) Is not an IHE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Award (NoA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The official, legally binding document, signed (or electronic equivalent) by a Grants Management Officer that outlines budgetary information as well as standard and specific award conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally the NoA: (1) notifies the recipient of the award; (2) contains or references all terms and conditions of the grant including specific conditions and Federal funding limits and obligations; (3) documents the basis for recording the obligation of Federal funds in the NIH accounting system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) / Parent announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: A publicly available document by which a Federal Agency makes known its intentions to award discretionary grants or cooperative agreements, usually as a result of competition. NIH NOFOs may be known as program announcements, requests for applications, notices of funding availability, solicitations, or other names. Parent announcement (broad NOFO) enables investigator-initiated applications for a specific activity code (e.g., Parent R01).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NOFOs can be found at Grants.gov and naming conventions vary by agency/program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: When used in connection with a non-Federal entity’s utilization of funds under a Federal award, obligations means orders placed for property and services, contracts and subawards made, and similar transactions during a given period that require payment by the non-Federal entity during the same or a future period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Management and Budget (OMB)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Office of the President, Office of Management and Budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offset
rubrics_metrics.description: IC or awarding agency approval/authorization of the use of unobligated grant funds remaining from a prior budget period to support grant activities of the current budget period. An offset does not change the current budget period authorized amount of funding but reduces the amount of current fiscal year funds provided to support the authorized award amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Researcher and Contributor Identifiers (ORCID iDs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unique, persistent digital identifiers that distinguish individual investigators and can be used to connect researchers with their contributions to science over time and across changes of name, location, and institutional affiliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORCID iDs are free and assigned/maintained by the non-profit organization ORCID.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: A generic term used to refer to an Institution of Higher Education or other entity, including an individual, which applies for or receives an NIH grant or cooperative agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Significant Contributors (OSCs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals who have committed to contribute to the scientific development or execution of the project, but are not committing any specified measurable effort (i.e., person months) to the project. These individuals are typically presented at 'effort of zero person months' or 'as needed.' Individuals with measurable effort may not be listed as OSCs. Consultants should be included if they meet this definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other support
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes all resources made available to a researcher or senior key personnel in support of and/or related to all of their research endeavors, regardless of monetary value and regardless of whether they are based at the institution the researcher identifies for the current grant. Other support does not include training awards, prizes, start-up support from the US-based institution, or gifts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: (1) Gifts are resources provided where there is no expectation of anything in return. (2) Monetary donations to institutions or directly to senior/key personnel that support research activities related to an individual are given with an expectation and therefore must be reported as other support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oversight agency for audit
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal agency that provides the predominant amount of funding directly (direct funding) to a recipient or subrecipient as listed on the schedule of expenditures of Federal awards (see 2 CFR Part 200.510(b)), unless OMB designates a specific cognizant agency for audit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If direct funding represents less than 25% of total Federal expenditures, the predominant source of total funding (direct and subawards) is the designated cognizant agency. Duties and reassignment processes are described in 2 CFR Part 200.513(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant support costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct costs that support participants and their involvement in a Federal award such as stipends, subsistence allowances, travel allowances, registration fees, temporary dependent care, and per diem paid directly to or on behalf of participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Kirschstein-NRSA programs and Education Grants (e.g., R25), this term does not apply; NIH will continue to use terms trainees, trainee-related expenses, and trainee travel for those programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pass-through entity
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-Federal entity that provides a subaward to a subrecipient (including lower tier subrecipients) to carry out part of a Federal program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authority of the pass-through entity under this part flows through the subaward agreement between the pass-through entity and subrecipient. See 2 CFR 200.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payback
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that the recipient of an NRSA postdoctoral fellowship engage in qualified health-related research, training, or teaching activities for a length of time equal to the period of NRSA support received. Only the first year of training incurs a payback obligation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In general, payback activity must involve at least 20 hours per week and be conducted over 12 consecutive months; special exceptions may be considered case-by-case. See Ruth L. Kirschstein NRSA—Payback for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment Management System
rubrics_metrics.description: The HHS centralized grants payment system operated by the Payment Management Service, Program Support Center. Most HHS (and some other Federal) recipients receive grant payments through this system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: The two-stage process that involves consistent application of standards and procedures to produce fair, equitable, timely, and objective examinations of applications based on evaluation of scientific or technical merit or other relevant aspects. Review is performed by experts (Peer Reviewers) in the field for which support is requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review provides guidance and recommendations to NIH individuals responsible for making award decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of performance / Project period
rubrics_metrics.description: The time interval between the start and end date of a Federal award, which may include one or more budget periods. Identification of the period of performance in the Federal award does not commit the Federal agency to fund the award beyond the currently approved budget period. The period of performance for NIH awards is noted on the Notice of Award. The total project period comprises the initial competitive segment, any subsequent competitive segments resulting from renewals, and extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 'Project period' and 'Budget period' for related definitions; the project period does not constitute a commitment to fund beyond approved budget periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Person months
rubrics_metrics.description: The metric for expressing the effort (amount of time) PD/PI(s), faculty and other senior/key personnel devote to a specific project. Effort is based on the type of appointment (calendar year, academic year, summer term) and the organization's definition of such (e.g., academic year defined as 9- or 10-month appointment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal property
rubrics_metrics.description: Property of any kind except real property. It may be tangible, or intangible, such as copyrights, patents, or securities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personally Identifiable Information (PII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information that can be used to distinguish or trace an individual’s identity, alone or when combined with other personal or identifying information that is linked or linkable to a specific individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PII is not attached to any single category of information or technology; requires case-by-case assessment of identification risk. Non-PII can become PII when additional information is made publicly available that could be used to identify an individual when combined with other available information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase III clinical trial
rubrics_metrics.description: A broadly based prospective Phase III clinical investigation (usually involving several hundred or more human subjects) to evaluate an experimental intervention in comparison with a standard or control intervention or to compare two or more existing treatments. Includes pharmacologic, non-pharmacologic, and behavioral interventions for disease prevention, prophylaxis, diagnosis, or therapy. Community trials and other population-based intervention trials are included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See clinical trial definition for context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-award costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Any cost incurred prior to the beginning date of the project period or the initial budget period of a competitive segment (under a multi-year award), in anticipation of the award and at the applicant’s own risk, for otherwise allowable costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Written approval obtained in advance by an authorized official of a Federal agency or pass-through entity of certain costs or programmatic decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Administrative Requirements—Changes in Project and Budget—Prior Approval Requirements for specific actions requiring prior approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profit
rubrics_metrics.description: See definition for fee (fee defined elsewhere in policy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Program
rubrics_metrics.description: A coherent assembly of plans, project activities, and supporting resources contained within an administrative framework, whose purpose is to implement an organization’s mission or some specific program-related aspect of that mission. For the NIHGPS, 'program' refers to NIH programs that carry out their missions through awarding grants or cooperative agreements to other organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Director/Principal Investigator (PD/PI)
rubrics_metrics.description: The individual(s) designated by the applicant organization/recipient to have the appropriate level of authority and responsibility to direct the project or program to be supported by the award. The applicant organization may designate multiple PD/PIs who share authority and responsibility; when multiple PD/PIs are named, each is responsible and accountable for proper conduct of the project, including submission of required reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of multiple PD/PIs does not diminish the responsibility or accountability of any individual PD/PI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program income
rubrics_metrics.description: Gross income earned by the recipient or subrecipient that is directly generated by a supported activity or earned as a result of the Federal award during the period of performance, except as provided in 2 CFR Part 200.307(f). Includes income from fees for services, use/rental of property acquired under Federal awards, sale of fabricated items, license fees and royalties, and principal/interest on loans made with Federal award funds. Interest earned on advances of Federal funds is not program income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except as provided, program income does not include rebates, credits, discounts, and interest earned on them. See applicable CFR sections and 35 USC §§ 200-212 for inventions under Federal awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Official/Program Officer/Project Officer
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH official responsible for the programmatic, scientific, and/or technical aspects of a grant or cooperative agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progress report
rubrics_metrics.description: A periodic, usually annual report submitted by the recipient and used by NIH to assess progress and, except for the final progress report of a project period, to determine whether to provide funding for the subsequent budget period. May also be called the non-competing continuation progress report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project/performance site
rubrics_metrics.description: Location(s) where the work described in the research plan will be conducted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Property
rubrics_metrics.description: Real property or personal property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protected Personally Identifiable Information (Protected PII)
rubrics_metrics.description: PII (see PII), except for PII that must be disclosed by law. Examples include social security number, passport number, credit card numbers, clearances, bank numbers, biometrics, date and place of birth, mother’s maiden name, criminal, medical and financial records, and educational transcripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questioned cost
rubrics_metrics.description: An amount, expended or received from a Federal award, that in the auditor’s judgment: (i) is noncompliant or suspected noncompliant with Federal statutes, regulations, or award terms; (ii) at the time of the audit, lacked adequate documentation to support compliance; or (iii) appeared unreasonable and did not reflect actions a prudent person would take in the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: (2) calculation method for (1)(ii) if portion lacking documentation is confirmed non-compliant; (3) there is no questioned cost solely because of internal control deficiencies or certain reporting noncompliance if it does not affect amounts expended/received; (4) 'known questioned cost' defined as specifically identified by auditor; (5) 'likely questioned cost' is auditor’s best estimate extrapolated from audit evidence; (6) questioned costs are not improper payments until reviewed and confirmed per OMB Circular A–123 Appendix C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real property
rubrics_metrics.description: Land, including land improvements, structures and appurtenances thereto, and legal interests in land, including fee interest, licenses, rights of way, and easements. Excludes moveable machinery and equipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient
rubrics_metrics.description: An entity that receives a Federal award directly from a Federal agency to carry out an activity under a Federal program. The term recipient does not include subrecipients, consortiums or individuals that are participants or beneficiaries of the award. See Non-Federal entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal application
rubrics_metrics.description: An application requesting additional funding for a period subsequent to that provided by a current award. Renewal applications compete for funds with all other peer-reviewed applications and must be developed as fully as though applying for the first time. The previous NIH term was 'competing continuation.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal award
rubrics_metrics.description: A Federal award for which the start date is contiguous with, or closely follows, the end of the expiring Federal award. The start date of a renewal award begins a new and distinct period of performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research & Development (R&D)
rubrics_metrics.description: All basic and applied research activities, and all development activities performed by HHS award recipients. 'Research' is systematic study directed toward fuller scientific knowledge or understanding; 'Development' is systematic use of knowledge to produce useful materials, devices, systems, or methods, including prototypes and processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes activities involving training of individuals in research techniques when such activities use the same facilities and are not part of instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Administrator
rubrics_metrics.description: Acts as a local agent of the Authorized Organizational Representative (AOR) and/or PD/PIs providing day-to-day grant-related support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Roles and Responsibilities—Recipient Staff for further detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Fabrication, falsification, or plagiarism in proposing, performing, or reviewing research, or in reporting research results. Fabrication = making up data/results and recording/reporting them. Falsification = manipulating research materials, equipment, or processes, or changing/omitting data or results so research is not accurately represented. Plagiarism = appropriation of another person’s ideas, processes, results, or words without appropriate credit. Research misconduct does not include honest error or differences of opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research patient care costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs of routine and ancillary services provided by hospitals to participants in research protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible party
rubrics_metrics.description: Term used in Title VIII of FDAAA (2007) to refer to the entity or individual responsible under FDAAA for registering a clinical trial and submitting clinical trial information to ClinicalTrials.gov.
